title: First communion
hookLine: a child's first time at the table, remembered for life

lines: A LINE OF CHILDREN, TWO BY TWO.
HANDS HELD THE WAY THEY PRACTICED.
A PIECE OF BREAD, THE SIZE OF A COIN.
cards: A line of children walks up the aisle, two by two. Some girls in white dresses, a few with veils that keep slipping. Boys in shirts buttoned to the top, which they'll undo the second this is over.

Grandparents twisting around in the pews with phones up. Each child has practiced this: hands held a certain way, the right answer to say. Then one small girl reaches the front, and it isn't practice anymore.
A piece of bread the size of a coin, and a word spoken just to her. Years later she might not remember the homily. She'll probably remember the dress.

teach.h: A CHILD'S FIRST TIME AT THE TABLE.
teach.b: First communion means a child's first time receiving the bread, and in some churches the cup, at the Lord's table. When depends on the church.
In Catholic parishes, a child is usually baptized as a baby and receives first communion later in childhood, after classes, often with a family celebration.
The Orthodox do it differently. As yesterday showed, an Orthodox baby is baptized and anointed in one service, and can receive communion right away, a tiny spoonful of bread and wine.
So a child raised Orthodox won't remember a first communion; there was never a time they weren't at the table. Protestant churches vary.
Some wait until a child is confirmed, some until a child can say what the meal means, and some welcome any baptized child. Each way has a page it leans on.
Those who wait often point to Paul: "let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup." Those who welcome the very young often point to Mark.
People bring little children to Jesus, and the disciples tell them off.
"But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God."

Underneath both, a psalm: "O taste and see that the LORD is good." Taste: a mouth, a piece of bread, a first time. Each of these churches is trying to do right by that taste, and they disagree, in earnest, about when.

how: Catholic children usually receive first communion in childhood after a period of preparation, often in a parish celebration; Orthodox Christians receive from infancy; Protestant churches differ, some after confirmation, some when a child can understand, some at any age after baptism.

games.q: people are bringing little children to Jesus, and his disciples are telling them off. what does Jesus do?
o: agree, and keep teaching the adults.
he's much displeased, and tells them to let the children come.
say the children can come back when they're older.
games.why: "he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not." some churches lean on this scene to welcome the very young to the table.

practice: Let one first time come back to you: a first communion if you had one, a first meal in a new home, the first time someone let you sit at the grown-ups' table. Go slowly: what you wore, who was near, what it tasted like.
If you pray, thank God for the person who brought you to that table; if you don't, just thank them in your mind.

wordCard.voice: First communion. A child's first time at the Lord's table, which comes at different ages in different churches.
